items.title: Behind the build: Generative plugins and shaders at Figma
items.excerpt: Rogie King walks through how Figma built generative plugins and shaders, giving designers programmatic and creative control over generated visuals on the canvas — and a way to share what they make with the community.
items.why: Generative output moves from a prompt box into a scriptable, shareable plugin/shader layer — designers get parameters and reuse instead of one-off generations.

items.title: The case against intuitive design in enterprise software
items.excerpt: Eric Chung argues that 'intuitive' is the wrong target for enterprise tools, where expert users need dense, learnable interfaces rather than instantly-obvious ones.
items.why: Directly reframes a default heuristic designers apply — relevant as AI-generated UI keeps optimizing for surface simplicity over expert throughput.

items.title: Graphic designers are trying to fix people's terrible AI flyers
items.excerpt: A viral trend has professional designers redoing the AI-generated flyers people post online, turning the gap between generated output and finished craft into public before/after evidence.
items.why: A concrete, visual argument about what generation still can't do — typography, hierarchy, print craft — framed as a designer's job, not a lament.

items.title: A viral creative challenge just gifted Parker pens the perfect anti-AI billboard advert
items.excerpt: A viral rebranding challenge produced an ad concept that positions the humble pen against AI-generated everything, and it's landing harder than most agency work.
items.why: Shows the creative positioning designers are reaching for in an AI-saturated market — a craft/authorship pitch, not a tooling one.

items.title: Is Nvidia's DLSS 5 an AI slop machine or a game-changing technology?
items.excerpt: Creative Bloq weighs whether DLSS 5's neural rendering brings real-time graphics closer to the artist's original intent or just invents pixels nobody authored.
items.why: Neural upscaling now decides what a large share of rendered frames actually look like — an authorship question aimed squarely at 3D/real-time artists.

items.title: One-Click Line Art From Any 3D Model In Blender
items.excerpt: Masamune Sakaki released a free Blender tool that turns any 3D model into clean line art in a single click, replacing a fiddly Grease Pencil / Freestyle setup.
items.why: A deterministic, free shortcut for a look designers usually fake with generation — 3D-to-2D stylization with exact control.

items.title: Check Out This Plug-In for C4D & Blender That Creates Realistic Damage
items.excerpt: Edgy is a new plug-in for Cinema 4D and Blender that generates realistic wear and damage on models, shipping with six ready-made setups plus authoring for custom ones.
items.why: Procedural detailing where designers would otherwise prompt or hand-sculpt — presets as a controllable middle ground.

items.title: Get Free Access To Over 70 Shader Tutorials
items.excerpt: XorDev opened up a library of 70+ shader tutorials for free, covering the math and tricks behind procedural visual effects.
items.why: Shader literacy is the counterweight to prompt-only visuals — writing the effect instead of sampling it.

items.title: Text-to-CAD Isn't Text-to-Mesh: Why the Output Format Is the Whole Story
items.excerpt: A breakdown of why 'AI CAD' demos that emit meshes don't help engineers: without parametric, editable B-rep output, the generated geometry can't be revised or manufactured.
items.why: The editability question — mesh vs. parametric — is the same one facing every design-to-X tool: does the AI hand you an artifact you can keep working in?

items.title: Siemens launches Eigen Engineering Agent in Thailand
items.excerpt: Siemens rolled out its Eigen Engineering Agent, an AI assistant aimed at engineering and design workflows, into a new market.
items.why: Agentic assistance moving into mainstream industrial design/engineering toolchains, not just consumer creative apps.

items.title: Additive research update: sensors, sustainability, and single-shot shapes
items.excerpt: A roundup of new additive manufacturing research, including embedded sensors, more sustainable feedstocks, and parts printed as a single shot rather than assembled.
items.why: Fabrication constraints are the real boundary on generative/topology-optimized geometry — this is what widens it.

items.title: What's !important #18: <geolocation>, Syntax ::highlight()ing, named-feature(), and More
items.excerpt: Daniel Schwarz's roundup of emerging CSS and web platform features, including new selectors and feature-query syntax landing in browsers.
items.why: The primitives designers and their coding agents will actually be able to reach for next — platform capability, not tooling hype.

items.title: AI can write SVG. Only one route gives you paths you can edit.
items.excerpt: A chatbot writes SVG markup blind, an image model gives you pixels, and a vector generator gives you paths — the piece compares what each route actually outputs and how to check the file before shipping it.
items.why: Practical triage for anyone generating icons or logos: three routes that look identical in a preview and are wildly different the moment you need to edit.

items.title: Design to Code Tools Benchmark [2026]: 5 Tools, Real Diffs
items.excerpt: The same messy SaaS dashboard was pushed through five design-to-code tools and scored on accessibility, semantics, bundle size, editability, and visual fidelity, with a reproducible harness.
items.why: Moves the design-to-code argument off screenshots and onto measurable diffs — the sort of evidence design orgs need before standardizing on one.

items.title: Software engineers' new job isn't writing code — it's designing the boundaries AI agents can't break
items.excerpt: As agents take over micro-logic, the job shifts to defining guardrails, data contracts, and feedback loops that keep generated systems reliable.
items.why: The same role shift is hitting design: authoring constraints and systems the agent must respect, rather than authoring every screen.

items.title: fx is now available in the AI SDK harness layer
items.excerpt: Vercel added an @ai-sdk/harness-fx adapter built on the ACP harness, letting another coding agent plug into the same AI SDK harness interface.
items.why: The harness layer is becoming a swappable socket — teams can change which agent builds their UI without rewriting the pipeline around it.

items.title: Set per-user budgets on AI Gateway
items.excerpt: Vercel's AI Gateway now supports individual spend limits per team member, so orgs can cap what each person's agent runs cost.
items.why: Token budget is now a design-team resource question — who on the team gets how much generative headroom becomes a governance decision.

items.title: Empire At Sea Brings A Shared Mixed Reality Drama To Venice Immersive
items.excerpt: Empire At Sea debuts at Venice Immersive as a shared mixed-reality drama where an audience experiences the piece together in one physical space.
items.why: Co-located mixed reality is a distinct design problem from solo headset work — staging, sightlines, and shared attention rather than a single viewport.

items.title: 'Neon Genesis Evangelion' VR is Getting First Public Preview Sept 25
items.excerpt: The Evangelion VR project opens its first public preview later this month, giving outsiders their first hands-on with how the anime's cockpit and scale are translated to a headset.
items.why: An adaptation problem designers care about: how a strongly-authored 2D visual language survives being reprojected into embodied space.

items.title: 9 Designs That Inspired Meshtimes, One of Tech's Most Creative Minds | Source Material
items.excerpt: Figma's Source Material series walks through nine designs that shaped one of tech's most creative practitioners, tracing where a visual sensibility actually comes from.
items.why: Taste as an assembled reference library — the input side of design work that generation can't shortcut.

items.title: The Making of i-D Magazine's 375 "The Beta Issue" - Designed in Figma
items.excerpt: A behind-the-scenes look at how i-D's 375th issue, 'The Beta Issue,' was art-directed and laid out entirely in Figma.
items.why: A screen tool used end-to-end for print editorial — a concrete case of the design toolchain collapsing into one canvas.

items.title: The One-Prompt Dashboard Trick
items.excerpt: Matt Wolfe demonstrates building a working data dashboard from a single prompt, showing how far one-shot generation gets you before hand-editing starts.
items.why: A blunt demo of where prompt-to-UI actually lands today, and what a designer still has to take over afterward.
